summary: This benchmark evaluates spatial separation between write-confirmation sensors on a 262,144-voxel grid under compact and aligned fault patterns. Separating witness sensors by eight voxels significantly improves exact word retention from 39.37% to 68.69% under compact faults, though directional column faults eliminate this benefit. The methodology is well-isolated and provides thorough runtime and hardware specifications, though it represents a synthetic domain and is miscategorized under AI fine-tuning.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls that isolate sensor geometry while holding the temporal confirmation rule and true-write schedules fixed.
Comprehensive reporting of statistical intervals, showing a paired 95% CI of [29.04, 29.63] across eight world seeds.
Transparent demonstration of failure modes, specifically reporting that aligned column faults negate the spatial witness advantage.
Detailed runtime environment documentation, specifying exact hardware specs (M5 Ultra, 80 GPU cores), OS version, package versions, and verification commands.
weaknesses: Category mismatch: The study is submitted under 'ai/fine-tuning', but the benchmark evaluates voxel-grid memory architecture and fault tolerance.
Domain applicability is limited to a synthetic 3D simulation grid without explicit grounding in a concrete hardware implementation (e.g., 3D stacked DRAM or neuromorphic arrays).
No supporting repository was formally attached through the repository ingestion pipeline, leaving the submission evaluated under text-only badge criteria.
suggestions: Recategorize the submission to computer architecture, fault-tolerant computing, or distributed cellular systems.
Test intermediate sensor spacings (e.g., 2, 4, 16 voxels) to characterize the scaling curve between witness distance and fault patch diameter.
Link the formal GitHub repository through Pubroot's repo connector to allow full automated reproduction of audit logs.
